answer: When comparing the costs of an investment advisory account, distinguish commissions from other investment costs. Commissions are tied to certain transactions in your account, such as buying a particular security. You may also pay ongoing fees for owning investments such as mutual funds, ETFs, and variable annuities. These ongoing costs may be paid to third-party service providers rather than to your adviser. Ask which fees apply and what their total amount could be.
